_doc: Where a reader marked Glessner's facial landmarks on the 1910 plate, in pixels of the crop `crop_px` (left, top, right, bottom) of the scan, after a 1.6 px Gaussian blur that removes the halftone screen. `sigma_px` is the reader's own uncertainty: the pupils are the catchlights' centres; the eye corners sit behind the spectacle rims; the mouth and the lip line are under the moustache; the chin's lower edge meets the collar's shadow; the ear is in shadow; the crown's top is the bald scalp's outline, under a little white hair. tools/fit_portrait_face.py fits the face to these marks.
age_note: The photograph is undated and was printed in 1910, when he was 67. It is fitted as his face at the scene date (61, from born 1843): between 61 and 67 the renderer's ageing pair moves these landmarks by under a millimetre, far inside the marks' uncertainty.
basis: Fitted to a photograph of him showing his whole face (the 1910 Commercial Club plate): the eye spacing, nose, mouth, chin and ear placement are read from it, as far as the shared MakeHuman face axes can express them. Depth is read from a single quarter view, so an axis the marks say little about stays near the town's average (listed as mostly_prior).
not_modelled: his colouring (the plate is a monochrome halftone; skin, hair and cloth colours are chosen)

card._doc: What the person's card shows (T-3413): `portrait` is cut from the scan at `portrait_from_scan_px` (left, top, right, bottom) and scaled to `size_px`; `model` is tools/portrait_still.mjs's render of the fitted face on `body`, turned to the fit's yaw and framed like the portrait. `dress` (T-3440): the still is dressed as humans.js dresses him in town, with his skin, his own hair and moustache (human-hair-styles.js) and his spectacles (human-spectacles.js). `hide` leaves out his derby: the portrait is bareheaded.
